paragraphs: Friend, here's what I take from Athens. Paul was in a city full of idols, and he didn't hide and he didn't just fume. He talked to people in the synagogue and in the marketplace, and then he stood up in front of the sharpest crowd in town. He started with something they already knew, an altar "TO AN UNKNOWN GOD," and told them the God they were guessing at has a name and has made Himself known (Acts 17:16-23).

Now look at what Paul says about this God. He made the world and everything in it, and He "does not live in temples made by human hands" (Acts 17:24). He doesn't need our help, because "He Himself gives everyone life and breath and everything else" (Acts 17:25). And He is "not far from each one of us," because "in Him we live and move and have our being" (Acts 17:27-28). So nothing made of gold or silver or stone can stand in for Him, and the whole world is invited to turn to Him.

And that turning is the point. God "now commands all people everywhere to repent," because He has set a day to judge the world with justice by the Man He appointed, and He gave proof by raising Him from the dead (Acts 17:30-31). Some mocked, some wanted to hear more, and some believed (Acts 17:32-34). Friend, the same call applies to everyone, and what you do with it is the question, so lean in, ask for more, and let it change you.
